headline: Approved wine license for GILT at 11 Lexington Ave. with a 40-hour weekly requirement, plus George's Restaurant hours change at 178 Washington St.
summary: Approved a new seasonal wine-only license for GILT at 11 Lexington Ave., a change of hours for George's Restaurant and Bar at 178 Washington St., and a one-day wine and malt permit for a wedding at 24 Hough Ave. Also voted to advertise applications for one annual all-alcohol license from September 21 to September 28, 2026.
decisions: Approved a new Annual, Section 15 Seasonal, Wine Only License for Laura Lee, dba GILT, at 11 Lexington Ave., with conditions to be open 40 hours a week and complete an updated financials page, 3-0.
Approved a change of hours for J & Z Gloucester Foods LLC, dba George's Restaurant and Bar, at 178 Washington St., 3-0.
Approved a one-day permit to serve wine and malt beverages only at a wedding on 9/12/2026 from 5:00 PM to 8:00 PM at 24 Hough Ave., 3-0.
Approved advertising a legal notice that applications for one annual all-alcohol license will be accepted from Monday, September 21st through Monday, September 28th, 3-0.

All in favor, 3-0

plain_text:
CITY OF GLOUCESTER 
                                               LICENSING BOARD MEETING 
 
City Hall Conference Room 
City Hall, 1st Floor 
    9 Dale Avenue 
Gloucester, MA 01930 
 
Meeting Minutes  
September 8, 2026 
 
 
Board Members Present: 
 
Melissa J. Teixeira Prince, Chairperson  
John Lamirande  
Ted Costa 
 
Also in Attendance: 
Natasha Dale, Licensing Board Clerk  
Rob Vicari, Building Commissioner  
 
 
 
The Chair Calls to Order the Quorum of the Licensing Board at 6:30 PM. 
 
The Chair reads the following statement; 
 Effective August 16, 2023 the public is welcome to attend our meetings in person. 
Alternatively, the public may attend through the zoom link listed on the agenda. The 
meeting notice will reflect if this a meeting of zoom only. As the recent amendments to 
the Open Meeting Law allows the Committee can continue to hold the meeting remotely. 
Please note that the in person meeting will not be suspended or terminated if 
technological problems interrupt the remote connection.  
 
Public Hearing: 
 
Petition of Laura Lee, dba GILT on a proposed new Annual, Section 15 Seasonal, Wine 
Only License at 11 Lexington Ave. Manager of Record: Laura Lee 
 
Laura Lee, 92 Main St., Gloucester is present. 
 
Ms. Lee currently owns The Cave in downtown Gloucester and is planning to keep both 
businesses at the same time with intentions of closing down the Main St. location as she 
gets closer to retirement.
Her new business will be GILT. This will feature gift baskets, vintage clothes and wine. 
There will not be a cheese counter as part of the plan for the immediate future. Chocolate 
and cookies will be prepackaged. 
 
Ms. Lee states that once fully opened she would be open to having a few wine tastings.  
 
Ms. Lee states t hat she believes the wine will be 15 -20% of the total square footage. The 
total square footage is 1,100 square feet.  
 
Ms. Lee primarily wants to open this business for gift baskets and is anticipating to be 
open 7 days a week. 
 
Lexington Ave. is quiet during January, February and March. But the store will see a lot 
of foot traffic.  
 
Ms. Lee does not see having more than 12 cases of wine at a time in the store. The rest of 
the store will be basket items.  
 
Ms. Lee would be sellin g a different selection of wines and champagnes than the variety 
store that has a package store license down the street has. Ms. Lee is planning to sell more 
“boutique” wines that you cannot find at the convenient stores.  
 
Ms. Lee is planning on having a friend help out at The Cave while she opens and settles 
into GILT. 
 
There will be little to no competition in the Magnolia area for this type of store.  
 
The chair opens the public hearing. 
Speaking in favor: none 
Speaking in opposition: none 
The chair closes the public hearing. 
 
Ms. Prince states that she at first was not in support of the project, but as the presentation 
went on she is now on board. She believes that this is something different for the area. 
But Ms. Prince does have concerns at how many h ours Ms. Lee would be open. Ms. Lee 
agreed to be open for 40 hours a week. 
 
Mr. Costa moves to approve the Petition of Laura Lee, dba GILT on a proposed new 
Annual, Section 15 Seasonal, Wine Only License at 11 Lexington Ave. Manager of 
Record: Laura Lee with the conditions that she be open 40 hours a week and an updated 
financials page on her application needs to be complete. 
 
Mr. Lamirande seconds 
All in favor, 3-0 
 
Continued Business:
Petition of Zorba Kinigstein on a change of hours for J & Z Gloucester Foods LLC, dba 
George’s Restaurant and Bar, 178 Washington St. 
 
Joel Favazza, Seaside Legal Solutions, 123 Main St., Gloucester is present representing 
his client.  
Zorba Kinigstein, 594 Western Ave., Gloucester is present.  
 
This is a continued hearing regarding the change of hours for George’s Restaurant. Mr. 
Favazza states that dinner service is being eliminated and he is proposing to be open for 
alcohol sales Monday- Saturday 8:00 AM- 3:00 and Sundays from 10:00 AM- 4:00 PM. 
 
Breakfast and lunch will still be served daily.  
 
Mr. Favazza states that after George’s closes there is no shortage of restaurants that 
serve alcohol for dinner service. But on the flip side, there are not a lot of restaurants 
that serve alcoholic beverages for breakfast.  
 
The sale of alcohol has gone from 11% to 8.5%.  
 
Mr. Favazza states that dinner was not the largest money maker for the restaurant. If 
Mr. Kinigstein finds reliable help he can open back up for dinner.  
 
At this time Mr. Kinigstein is trying to stay in compliance with the ABCC in terms of his 
hours.  
 
Mr. Kinigstein states that it is extremely difficult to find help at the moment. He is 
looking for another daytime cook as well as a night time cook to open back up for dinner 
again. To open for dinner, Mr. Kinigstein would need three cooks and wait staff.  
 
George’s has served 52,500 guests so far this year. Last year George’s served 65,500 
total. 
 
Mr. Kinigstein only has one shift of employees who work 9 and a half hour days.  
 
Mr. Costa moves to approve the petition of Zorba Kinigstein on a change of hours for J & 
Z Gloucester Foods LLC, dba George’s Restaurant and Bar, 178 Washington St. 
 
Mr. Lamirande seconds 
All in favor, 3-0 
 
Special One Day Liquor License Applications: 
 
Petition of Amber Fritsch requesting to serve wine and malt beverages only during a 
wedding on 9/12/2026 from 5:00 PM- 8:00 PM at 24 Hough Ave.  
 
Paul Tenhope, 45 Corning St., Beverly is present.
Mr. Tenhope works for Timothy S. Hopkins LLC Caterting out of Essex, MA. They are a 
12C caterer.  
 
Mr. Tenhope is catering an event from 4:30-7:30 at Stage Fort Park. It is a celebration of 
marriage for approximately 120 guests with beer, wine and mocktails.  
 
The alcohol will be in the designated guest tent with a bar setup. There will be 3 
bartenders working. Alcohol is packaged out the catering facility and is brought back 
with them at the end of the event.  
 
Staff will be monitoring guests for over consumption. The tent will have sidewalls 
installed to keep guests from roaming.  
 
Mr. Costa moves to approve the petition of Amber Fritsch requesting to serve wine and 
malt beverages only during a wedding on 9/12/2026 from 5:00 PM- 8:00 PM at 24 
Hough Ave.  
 
Mr. Lamirande seconds 
All in favor, 3-0 
 
 
Discussion by the Board: 
 
The Licensing Board will discuss the availability of 1 (one) Annual All-Alcohol On-
Premise License.  The Board will also discuss and establish a timeline for the application 
process, including the opening and closing dates for the acceptance of applications, the 
review process, and any related procedural deadlines.   
Applicants who are interested in the new annual year round license apply and all 
applications will be heard at our next meeting on October 13, 2026 with a decision being 
made on October 19, 2026 at 6:30 on a zoom meeting.  
An advertisement will be placed in the Gloucester Daily Times on Friday, September 11, 
2026 stating that the Licensing Board will be accepting applications for a new Annual 
All Alcohol liquor license from Monday, September 21, 2026 through Monday, 
September 28, 2026. 
Ms. Prince moves to advertise a legal notice on September 11th stating we have a license 
available and applications will be accepted from Monday, September 21st through 
Monday, September 28th with the hours being Mon-Thurs 8:30-3:30, Friday 8:30-12.  
Mr. Costa seconds 
All in favor, 3-0 
Adjournment:  
 
Mr. Costa moves to adjourn at: 8:31 PM
Mr. Lamirande seconds 
All in favor, 3-0
